thread:
emily chen: Quick question — trying to wire a service account token into a sidecar via values in an umbrella chart. I set `global.serviceAccount.name: my-app-sa` in the top-level values and expected subchart to pick it up, but the rendered env var still points to the autogenerated name. Anyone seen this?

raj patel: Do you have the subchart using `{{ default .Values.serviceAccount.name .Values.global.serviceAccount.name }}` or something similar? Helm scoping can be weird with umbrella vs subchart.

emily chen: Here's the relevant bits from values.yaml and the subchart template:
```yaml
# umbrella values.yaml
global:
  serviceAccount:
    name: my-app-sa
subchart:
  serviceAccount:
    create: false
```
and template in subchart: `envFrom: - secretRef: name: {{ .Values.serviceAccount.tokenSecret | default (printf "%s-token" .Release.Name) }}`

sam taylor: If subchart sets `create: false` it won't create the SA, but it should still reference `.Values.global.serviceAccount.name` unless the subchart template is only looking at `.Values.serviceAccount.*`. Many charts intentionally keep serviceAccount scoped to chart to avoid collisions.

emily chen: Right — I tried `subchart.serviceAccount.name: {{ .Values.global.serviceAccount.name }}` in umbrella, but Helm doesn't let you use templates inside values.yaml. So I put `subchart.serviceAccount.name: "my-app-sa"` as a workaround. Wanted to avoid duplicating.

raj patel: Another pattern is to add a small helper in the subchart templates like: `{{- $sa := .Values.serviceAccount.name | default $.Values.global.serviceAccount.name }}` and then use `$sa` — that reads global from top-level because of the `$` root context.

emily chen: Ah nice — I didn't realize using `$` would reach the umbrella's global. I'll try that. Any gotchas with `automountServiceAccountToken`? We have it set to `false` in cluster-level defaults for tighter security.

sam taylor: If automount is false on the SA, projected `serviceAccountToken` volume or token secret won't be created. For projected tokens you need the SA to have `automountServiceAccountToken: true` or explicitly mount a projected token. If you rely on the old token secret pattern (`-token-XXXXX`), note Kubernetes deprecated that for bound service account tokens.

emily chen: Good to know. We're on k8s 1.25 so bound tokens are used. Our sidecar expects a token file at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. If `automountServiceAccountToken` is false on the pod spec, it won't be there.

raj patel: Two options: 1) Set `pod.spec.automountServiceAccountToken: true` in the chart when sidecar is enabled, or 2) explicitly create a projected volume using `serviceAccountToken` projection (recommended). The second is more explicit and works even if default is false.

emily chen: OK — I'll update subchart to use the `$` lookup for name and add a conditional projected volume for the token. Quick sanity check: if we use `lookup` to fetch a ServiceAccount resource in another namespace, we need cluster RBAC and the release namespace matters, right?

sam taylor: Yes, `lookup` is server-side and will fail during template rendering if Tiller/operator can't access cluster or has insufficient perms. For rendering at install time in CI you might not have cluster access. Prefer the `$` values pattern unless you need runtime discovery.

deploy-bot: PR #2345 opened by emily-chen: "subchart: read global SA name + add projected token mount" — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/helm-charts/pull/2345 :rocket:

emily chen: Thanks all. I'll push the PR with the helper change and the projected volume conditional, run integration, and tag for review. @raj @sam can you take a quick look when CI passes? :pray:
